tagline: Tobacco country turning to grapes, with Pilot Mountain looking on.
intro: The byway starts at Round Peak near Mount Airy and wanders by back roads to Dobson, down to the Yadkin at Rockford and on to Yadkinville, then west through the Swan Creek country to Elkin and north again to end at Zephyr. It is 76.5 miles of country road, about two hours.
Long tobacco country, it has been turning to vineyards. Pilot Mountain stays in view for much of the drive, a knob rising some 1,400 feet above the land around it.

moments.title: Round Peak
moments.text: The byway sets out from a community that gave its name to a style of old-time fiddle and banjo music, carried on by players such as Tommy Jarrell and Fred Cockerham.

moments.title: Pilot Mountain
moments.text: Off on the horizon stands Big Pinnacle, bare rock walls under a rounded green top, a core of quartzite left standing as the rest of the mountain wore away.

moments.title: Rockford
moments.text: The old Surry County seat on the Yadkin still has its former courthouse, and from 1900 a piano seller charged a quarter to cross his bridge, until 1930s floods took it.

sources.label: NCDOT, North Carolina Scenic Byways guidebook, Yadkin Valley Scenic Byway
